title: Machine identity creation guardrails and template registry
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Introduce server-side validation and a curated template registry for machine/service identities. Goals: reduce blast radius from over-privileged service accounts, make ownership explicit, enable fast self-service creation with enforceable least-privilege defaults, and emit structured audit events that tie creation/changes to SSO/SAML identities. This ticket covers the API/Console flow, template schema, enforcement hooks (admission controller + API validation), and audit log schema for RBAC v2 integration.
acceptance_criteria: Console + API allow creation only from approved templates or with a justification flag when policy permits
Each created identity must have an explicit owner field bound to a SAML or SCIM identifier; orphaned creations are blocked
Admission controller rejects requests that escalate privileges beyond template maxima
Creation/change events produce structured audit logs (JSON) with fields: actor_id, actor_type, template_id, requested_permissions, approved_permissions, request_id
Template registry accessible in Console with versioning and change history
Unit and integration tests for validation logic, and end-to-end test that verifies owner assignment via SSO identity
implementation_notes: Template schema: name, description, allowed_scopes, max_permissions_set, recommended_ttl, rotation_policy_hint
Enforcement points: API server validation layer, Kubernetes-style admission controller for on-prem deployments, and a Console pre-check UI
Audit logs will be ingested into our observability pipeline; add parsing rules in runtime-logs-index for downstream alerts
Owner resolution: map SAML Subject or SCIM user id to internal user record during token exchange; fallback to invitation workflow for external service principals
Migration: run a detection job to identify existing service accounts without owners and create remediation tickets
